findings.claim: The correction plans six independent project briefs and six topic labs—three for F10 and three for F16—but the approved model requires one reusable learner-facing project brief per calendar Project row. Java has two such rows, F10 and F16. Splitting each cohesive build into three artifacts duplicates the project artifact, fragments its scaffold and tests, and turns 53 topics into 59 rather than adding the two authorized day-level briefs.
findings.recommendation: Keep all six fixed syllabus concepts, but consolidate them into one canonical F10 brief/lab and one canonical F16 brief/lab. Each brief should map its day’s three curriculum pointers, state integrated outcomes and prerequisite/in-brief teaching order, and provide one starter scaffold plus one public Maven test suite. Standard and Fast overlays must reference these same canonical briefs rather than copies.

findings.claim: The canonical manifest order is F9, then all F11 topics inside classes-and-objects, then the new F10 classes-in-practice module. This contradicts the frozen F9–F10–F11 calendar sequence; the intake’s statement that module order is only authoring order conflicts with the repository contract that course.json and module.json carry order.
findings.recommendation: Represent F10 between F9 and F11 in canonical manifest traversal. Put the unified F10 project brief between those day groups in one module, or split the F9 and F11 groups into separate modules with the F10 module between them. Do not rely on prose outside the manifests to restore learner order.
